newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Packaging sees Q2 loss.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Packaging sees Q2 loss.

text.p: Integrated Packaging Assembly Corp Friday said it expects to report a loss of about $6.0 million, or $0.43 a share, after charges on revenues of about $4.0 million in the second quarter ended June 30.
The company said the loss stems from the company's dependence on a limited customer base and reduced orders from some of those clients during the quarter.

Integrated Packaging, an assembler of integrated circuit boards in the semiconductor industry, said it will cut 40 employees from its 188-person staff take a $3.0 million charge for impaired assets and severance.
Financial analysts had expected the company to report a loss of $0.12 a share, according to investment research firm First Call.
One year ago, Integrated Packaging generated a profit of $0.04 a share.
Integrated Packaging said it will continue focusing on sales and marketing to broaden its customer base and market segments.
Integrated Packaging currently focuses on graphics chipsets. Its sees telecommunications and field programmable gate array markets as areas it could expand into.
The majority of its staff cuts will come from manufacturing area, it said.
